content:
sara: Heads-up — we need to finalise per-org rate policy for RPM/TPM + concurrency. Product wants predictable SLAs, infra wants simple enforcement, and console needs a clean UX for telemetry.

josh: +1. Quick clarification: are we keeping both RPM (requests/min) and TPM (tokens/min) as primary knobs? Or collapse to one?

priya: We need both. RPM protects control plane/throughput, TPM protects cost (token-heavy requests). Examples: embeddings flood many tokens but few requests; chat spiky tokens.

ben: Concurrency caps are separate: limit simultaneous LBs per org to control QPS peaks and memory. Concurrency + TPM/RPM gives better isolation.

josh: Ok. Implementation question — enforcement at the edge (API gateway) vs at the runtime layer (model servers). Edge is fast for RPM but doesn't know token usage until runtime.

priya: Proposed hybrid: enforce RPM and concurrency at edge. Enforce TPM at runtime after token accounting; provide fast pre-check estimation for large streaming requests (client-specified max_tokens) to reject early.

ben: Edge-layer should support a small burst window (e.g., 30s) for short spikes. We'll track sliding-window counters and a token-leak algorithm to smooth. Burst budget per-org decays over time.

sara: UX: console should surface current RPM, TPM, concurrency usage and projected exhaustion time. Also show per-route breakdown and a ‘why I’m throttled’ reason with suggestion (reduce max_tokens, use embeddings batch).

josh: Telemetry: suggest these metric names — org.rate.rpm_used, org.rate.rpm_limit, org.tokens.tpm_used, org.tokens.tpm_limit, org.concurrency.current, org.burst.credit. Make alerts: 95th pct usage > 90% triggers paging for enterprise.

priya: Policy semantics: default tier = 100 RPM, 1M TPM, concurrency 20. Tiered plans override. Allow per-org overrides for special routes (e.g., embeddings-only endpoints get a different token-weight multiplier).

ben: Token weighting: treat embeddings tokens as 0.2x token-cost or better: actually embeddings are cheaper per-token but heavier per-request CPU — we should weight by cost estimate, not raw token count. Need a mapping table per model/route.

josh: Migration: current keys have simple per-key quota. Plan: map keys -> orgs, start enforcement in monitor mode for 2 weeks (log violations without rejecting), then soft-reject with 429 + 'quota_exceeded' header for a week, then hard-enforce.

sara: Rollout: canary 5 orgs (low-risk + one enterprise), then ramp 20%, 50%, 100% over 2 weeks. Provide self-serve override for sales for emergency bumps.

priya: Edge behaviour on streaming: allow initial chunk, estimate worst-case tokens if client omitted max_tokens, then progressively throttle if runtime reports > budget. Need to avoid mid-stream abrupt cutoffs.

ben: Grace policies: when org is at TPM limit, allow a short penalty box (reject for 10s) rather than long blocks; surface cooldown countdown to client. Also track 'grace uses' for orgs with transient spikes.

josh: Ops: add dashboard with per-org timeline and synthetic user to test throttle behaviour. Add ratebot alerts when an org enters >95% TPM for >5 minutes.

sara: Security: ensure rate metadata isn't spoofable. All org mappings validated server-side. No client-provided weights accepted.

priya: Open engineering questions: 1) exact burst window size, 2) token-weight table values, 3) default tier numbers, 4) DB for counters (redis vs in-memory + persistent sync).

ben: My opinion: use redis for fast counters + periodic writeback to clickhouse for audit/telemetry. Sliding window via fixed-size buckets to limit mem.

josh: I'll draft an RFC with these pieces and include sample HA configs, rules for canary and dashboards. Assign owners for the telemetry and console changes.

sara: Action items: @josh RFC by EOD Fri, @ben proto redis buckets + benchmark, @priya console mocks + messaging strings, ops team to prepare dashboard skeleton. I'll open the migration ticket and schedule canary list.

ratebot: Note: synthetic load test scheduled 2024-11-04T15:00Z; will create load org 'canary-rl' and run standard scenarios.

priya: Small UX note — add 'estimated exhaustion' tooltip that explains TPM vs RPM and recommends fixes.

josh: Thanks team. If no objections by EOD tomorrow we'll start work on the RFC and infra spikes.

ben: one more small item — add metric for 'throttled_by' label (rpm|tpm|concurrency|burst) to help triage.

sara: Good call. Closing thread for now, follow-ups in the RFC. :thumbsup:
